sources.title: Per Christian Hansen, Introduction to Inverse Problems, Chapter 4: Regularization Methods
sources.locator: Complete 29-slide chapter inspected. Slides 3–8 discuss ill-conditioning, TSVD, truncation and its bias; slides 11–17 give discrete Tikhonov with Hansen's lambda-squared penalty convention and its SVD filters; slides 21–23 give perturbation bounds; slides 25–29 discuss solution/residual behavior and the L-curve.
sources.independent_treatment: Hansen's DTU course notes; the second treatment is Clason's independent 119-page lecture notes.

contents.result: The SVD cutoff discards small singular directions, reducing noise amplification while introducing bias; the local item proves the exact cutoff-bias and retained-noise formulas.
contents.name: Slides 5–8: TSVD and truncated filter factors

contents.result: The finite-matrix perturbation discussion is used as independent context for separating the exact Tikhonov bias from data perturbation; the longer local chain and residual bounds are proved locally.
contents.name: Slides 11–17: discrete Tikhonov filter and perturbation context

contents.result: The condition-number and singular-value discussion motivates the explicit diagonal noise-amplification computation.
contents.name: Slides 3–5: ill-conditioning and singular directions

contents.result: The regularization-parameter discussion supports the example's separate bias and data-noise terms; the numeric values are verified locally.
contents.name: Slides 21–23: data and parameter perturbation context

sources.title: Per Christian Hansen, Introduction to Inverse Problems, Chapter 5: Regularization Parameter Choice
sources.locator: Complete 27-slide chapter inspected. Slides 2–6 state the data model and derive the finite-matrix forward-error split into regularization bias and data perturbation, including TSVD truncation; slides 7–27 discuss discrepancy, L-curve, cross-validation, GCV and normalized-periodogram criteria and their limitations.
sources.independent_treatment: Same DTU treatment as Chapter 4; used as an additional chapter, not counted as the independent second treatment.

contents.result: The slide-4 algebra is the finite-dimensional specialization of the local error chain; the local proof extends it with explicit operator-discretization and solve-residual terms.

contents.result: The slide-5 TSVD display supports keeping discarded-direction bias and retained-direction noise separate; the local item proves the threshold-convention version.

contents.result: The chapter treats discretized integral problems and distinguishes parameter-choice heuristics; the example's forward residual and its propagation are computed locally.

contents.result: The scalar residual calculation is proved in the example; the notes supply Tikhonov normal-equation context, not a floating-point residual certificate.

sources.title: Guido Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems, full lecture notes
sources.locator: Complete 119-page PDF fetched; relevant reasoning inspected in Chapters 2–3 on compact Hilbert-space operators and singular systems and Chapter 6, especially equations (6.1)–(6.4) and Theorem 6.5 with its proof (PDF pp. 56–63). Clason uses alpha as the coefficient of the squared penalty; it matches the local lambda convention directly.

contents.result: The Hilbert-space normal-equation characterization is inspected as context; the local proof establishes surjectivity and the inverse bound directly from coercivity and orthogonal decomposition.
